brief: Higher long-term rates have tightened financial conditions. Goldman's baseline has one more Fed hike in December, three cuts starting 2027H2, and 10-year yields easing from 5.3% to 4.4% by end-2027; it also gauges the drag if current rates persist instead. Three GDP channels drive the hit: residential investment is hit hardest, losing about 2pp of annualized growth at the 2026Q4 peak and 1pp on average in 2027 (mortgage lock-in: over 90% of borrowers sit below market rates), roughly double if rates stay at current levels. Consumer spending slows about 0.2pp in 2027 as durable-goods credit demand falls, partly offset by higher net interest income to net-lender households. Capex loses about 0.3pp in 2027 from refinancing costs, concentrated in small businesses (about half their debt is variable-rate); hyperscaler AI capex, by contrast, has stayed insensitive to rates and Goldman's strategists still expect a healthy 2027 pace. Net effect: GDP growth falls about 0.2pp in 2027 versus roughly 0.5pp if rates persist, still near 2.3% potential growth. Two added persistence risks: flat equities instead of the forecast +10% would cut consumption growth almost 0.5pp via wealth effects; and r-g turning positive by 2030 would push debt-to-GDP to 132% by 2035, 10pp above baseline, raising pressure for earlier deficit reduction.
